items.title: ✏️ You can finally edit the tracker prompt
items.body: The most-requested feature in DES. Prompts Editor → Tracker Prompt now shows the complete prompt exactly as the AI receives it — the instructions AND the JSON format specification that used to be generated-only and untouchable. Edit it and your version is sent word for word; leave it alone and DES keeps building it from your field settings as before, so fields you add later still get through. There's a live token estimate, an 'edited' badge, and a Restore Default button. Rename or remove a key and it warns you which panel goes blank when you do — because DES looks values up by key, and a silently empty Scene Tracker is a miserable thing to debug.

items.title: 🧩 Custom tracker fields, now with a shape
items.body: A custom Scene Tracker field used to be free text and nothing else — you described it and hoped the model answered in a usable form. Each one can now be Text, Number (with an optional range), Choice (you supply the options), List, Yes/No, or Percent, and the prompt tells the model exactly what to return instead of leaving it to chance. Custom fields also finally appear as on/off toggles in the Scene Tracker menu — that list was hardcoded before, so a field you created could never show up there. Existing fields are untouched and send exactly as they did.

items.title: 🛠️ New Workshop section in Settings
items.body: Relationships have moved out of a cramped tab in the Edit Trackers window and into their own section in the main menu. Add, rename and remove them freely, pick each one's card emoji from a click-to-choose grid, and turn the whole thing off if you don't use it. The list is generated from your config rather than hardcoded, so what you see is exactly what the AI is offered — and there's a new Wording box that lets you tell the model what the relationship actually means, with a live preview of the exact text it will receive.

items.title: 🎭 Your relationships now show up on character cards
items.body: The 'Relationship to player' row in the Character Workshop was five buttons written into the page — so a relationship you added was offered to the AI but could never be picked by hand. It's built from your list now, with your own additions on the end. Rather than growing taller with every one you add, it's a single row with arrows either side, and opening a card jumps straight to the relationship already set.

items.title: 🪟 The Edit Trackers window is a real working surface
items.body: It was capped at the width of a small dialog, which crushed each field — icon, name, AI instruction, type, delete — into a column barely wider than a phone. It's now up to 1080px, grouped into titled cards instead of one long run of rows, and two columns on a desktop window while stacking cleanly on a phone. The text boxes were also plain white on every dark theme (nothing in the stylesheet ever coloured them); they take your theme now. The Widgets section is gone — its toggles live in Settings → Scene Tracker, and four of the five did nothing anyway.

items.title: 🕐 The Scene Tracker stops vanishing
items.body: It was never actually deleted — it was being left behind on the previous message. The tracker skips redrawing when the scene hasn't changed, and that check only asked whether a header existed somewhere on the page, not whether it was still attached to the newest message. So any time two turns shared the same location and time (most turns), it stayed pinned to the older message and scrolled out of view. Toggling the feature off and on only seemed to fix it because that clears the cache. It follows the conversation down now.

items.title: 💬 Chat bubble text wraps around the portrait
items.body: The avatar used to own its own column, so anything longer than the portrait was squeezed into a narrow strip with a tall empty gutter sitting underneath it — very noticeable on phones and on long speeches. The text now runs alongside the portrait and flows underneath at full width once it clears the bottom. Both Discord and Card styles.

items.title: 📱 Two mobile annoyances fixed
items.body: The Mobile Compose Overlay opened on any focus of the message box — and SillyTavern focuses that box itself on page load, after sending, when a generation finishes, and whenever a popup closes. It now requires a real tap on the input, so it stops ambushing you on every reload. And the 'is this the same character?' popup was positioning itself against the wrong viewport on phones, sliding off the top of the screen with only its lower half visible; it now pins to what you can actually see and follows it as the browser chrome moves.
